thread:
tara (pm): Heads-up — Acme Fintech pushed a hard ask: on‑prem metrics export + per-route SLA controls. They said they'd sign a Dedicated contract if we can commit to these for their pilot. Do we fold into the coming release or scope it out?

mike (eng-lead): On‑prem metrics export is doable but not trivial. Need an agent to stream encrypted metrics offbox and a small schema change. Roughly 2 sprints + infra review.

alejandra (sales): They're on a tight procurement timeline, Q2 end. If we can't offer the SLA piece they'll go to VendorX. This is a high-ACV deal.

jordan (vp product): Tradeoff: take the deal & shift roadmap vs keep focus on platform-wide UX items that benefit many customers. Launch criteria for the Q2 release must be firm. My proposal: must-haves = secure export + per-route SLA controls for Dedicated pilots; nice-to-have = console policy editor polish.

chris (design): I can do a lightweight policy editor mock (30% fidelity) in a week: quick toggles for route priorities, SLA sliders, and an export toggle. Will post a prototype.

lee (ml infra): Per-route SLA routing means routing decisions at the proxy layer by cost/latency tier and fallback variants. That's coupled to the runtime. Adding that for Dedicated pilots will require kernel selection flags and telemetry hooks. I estimate 3 engineer-weeks + canary infra.

ana (solutions): Small correction — we already have a customer-configurable export in Private but it's not generalized. For Acme we could offer a specialized pilot config and charge for engineering hours.

alejandra (sales): If we can offer a pilot path (paid POC) with the two items and a clear ETA, they sign. They also asked for a simple SLA doc template.

mike (eng-lead): Path A: prioritize export + SLA for Dedicated pilots; ship minimal console UI (toggle + doc). Path B: delay SLA routing, ship export + policy API only, buy time with pilot contract. Path A = 4 wks sprint impact, Path B = 2 wks + more manual ops.

jordan (vp product): Decision time: do we accept the sprint hit for Path A? If yes, we spin up a focused squad and mark these as must-pass launch criteria for the Dedicated pilot. If no, offer Path B + compensating sales package. Thoughts?

chris (design): For speed, I prefer Path B UI-wise — API first, console polish later. We can reuse some existing controls.

lee (ml infra): Technically Path B is safest. It decouples runtime changes. We can implement routing rules as a config that the proxy evaluates without touching kernel selection for now.

ana (solutions): Recommend Path B + paid POC and a timeline that maps to their procurement. That buys us breathing room and keeps core roadmap intact.

alejandra (sales): I'll push for Path B but will tell them we have a prioritized plan for Path A if they want deeper SLAs later.

jordan (vp product): OK — tentative consensus Path B. Action items: 1) mike to scope export + policy API effort and ETA, 2) chris to deliver API-first mock + SLA doc template, 3) ana to draft pilot commercial terms, 4) ale to communicate plan to Acme with timeline. We'll revisit if Acme insists on Path A.

deploy-bot: New Confluence doc created: "Acme Dedicated pilot — export + per-route-policy (draft)" <https://confluence.internal/ACME-pilot>

tara (pm): Thanks — please add acceptance criteria to the doc: encryption-at-rest for exported metrics, per-route SLA fields, and roll-back plan. I'll set a follow-up sync Friday. :thumbsup:

mike (eng-lead): Will add the ETA and a minimal acceptance checklist.

chris (design): Mock link posted: <https://figma.internal/redwood/acme-policy-ui> — API-first flow sketched.

ana (solutions): I'll draft the pilot scope and estimate hours.

alejandra (sales): I'll send the customer the Path B proposal today and flag Path A options.

jordan (vp product): Good. This preserves our Q2 public roadmap while enabling a targeted enterprise win. Keep updates in that confluence doc.
